paper_id: Semantic-aware Contrastive Learning for Electroencephalography-to-Text Generation with Curriculum Learning
title: Semantic-aware Contrastive Learning for Electroencephalography-to-Text Generation with Curriculum Learning
motivation: Patients with neurological conditions need BCI to restore communication; current EEG-to-Text models suffer from subject-dependent representation drift.
problem_framing: EEG representations cluster by subject rather than by semantic content, causing many-to-one mapping problem and hindering cross-subject generalization.
key_insight: Use contrastive learning to pull same-sentence EEG across subjects together while pushing different-sentence EEG apart, with curriculum ordering from easy to hard pairs.
method_signature: C-SCL: contrastive pre-encoder training + seq2seq fine-tuning, with cosine-similarity-based curriculum levels for positive/negative pair difficulty.
evaluation_criteria: ROUGE, BLEU, and WER on ZuCo benchmark; ablation on single-subject, low-resource, and zero-shot settings.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Generated sentences still have spelling errors and fail to capture linguistic structure; large gap remains between generation and reference.
evidence_for_taste: nearly 45.93% of total constructed contrastive pairs already satisfy the final objective
directly leveraging hard pairs is quite challenging for the model learning
achieving a desirable semantic-dependent EEG representation space is a challenging task
easy pairs are insignificant but directly leveraging hard pairs is quite challenging
thinking_moves: 把subject-dependent representation drift问题重新frame成contrastive learning的pair construction问题
用t-SNE可视化原始EEG的subject clustering来诊断问题本质
从经验观察(45.93% pairs already satisfy)推断随机选择的冗余,提出curriculum筛选
证easy pairs和hard pairs各有缺陷,需要curriculum scheduler串联才能有效学习
通过单一curriculum level实验证明progressive learning的必要性
